Regulation: B.C. Reg. 92/2026
Made under: Liquor Control And Licensing Act
Published in: No. 10 – B.C. Regs. 83 to 93, June 2, 2026
Deposit date: May 29, 2026

B.C. Reg. 92/2026, deposited May 29, 2026, under theLIQUOR CONTROL AND LICENSING ACT[sections 80 and 83]. Order in Council 209/2026, approved and ordered May 29, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, (a)	the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 241/2016, is amended as set out in the attached Schedule, and (b)	effective June 1, 2029, Division 10 of Part 7 of the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation is repealed. — L. POPHAM,Minister of Agriculture and Food; L. BEARE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Part 7 of the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 241/2016, is amended by adding the following Division: Division 10 – Provisional Sales and Purchases "provisional purchaser"means a person who holds any of the following: (b)	a liquor primary club licence; (e)	a manufacturer licence endorsed with a lounge endorsement; "provisional seller"means a person who holds any of the following: (a)	a licensee retail store licence; (c)	a special wine store licence; (d)	a rural licensee retail store licence. Authorized provisional sales and purchases 206.3(1)	The licence of a provisional seller authorizes the licensee to sell liquor in unopened containers in the service area under the licence to a provisional purchaser. (2)	A provisional seller must not sell liquor under this section unless the provisional seller has first received from the provisional purchaser (a)	the provisional purchaser’s licence number, and (b)	any additional information the general manager may require. minutes_briefs.title: New B.C. rule lets liquor stores sell unopened bottles to clubs and lounges
minutes_briefs.summary: A new B.C. regulation creates a 'provisional sale' system. It lets certain liquor retailers (like licensee retail stores and special wine stores) sell unopened bottles of liquor directly to certain licence holders (like liquor primary clubs and manufacturers with a lounge endorsement). The seller must first get the buyer's licence number and any other required information. This is a new legal pathway for these sales, and the old rules in this part of the regulation are set to be removed in 2029.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you hold a qualifying liquor retail or club/lounge licence, review the new rules to see if you can use provisional sales and prepare to collect the buyer's licence number.

key_dates.label: New provisional sales rules take effect (B.C.)
